messages:
marta: Quick Q — working on SDK auth + error surface. How should we map API errors to exception types (401/403/429/5xx) and handle streaming disconnects? Also where do we attach request_id for debugging? I'm triaging token-refresh flakiness from mobile clients.

alex: Short answer: 401/403 -> AuthError (no automatic retry), 429 -> RateLimitError (honour Retry-After), 5xx -> ServerError / TransientServerError (retryable). Streaming disconnects should raise a StreamInterrupted/StreamError that contains partial payload + request_id so callers can decide to resume. Always include request_id as metadata on exceptions and in logs.

alex: Example mapping (py-like pseudo):
```py
if resp.status == 401:
    raise AuthError(msg, request_id=req_id)
if resp.status == 403:
    raise AuthError(msg, request_id=req_id)
if resp.status == 429:
    raise RateLimitError(msg, retry_after=resp.headers.get('Retry-After'), request_id=req_id)
if 500 <= resp.status < 600:
    raise ServerError(msg, transient=True, request_id=req_id)
```

cheng: For streaming specifically: do NOT swallow partial data. Emit a StreamError that contains the partial chunks and request_id. If a resume token is offered by the service, surface it on the error so clients can attempt resume. For websocket streams, try a single auth-refresh attempt then fail fast.

luisa: Logging guidance: always log structured entries with request_id. Example: `logger.debug('api call failed', extra={'request_id': req_id, 'stage': 'auth'})`. Also include the request_id on the exception object so Sentry/stack traces can link events back to infra logs.

sam: @alex can you open a tiny PR updating the mapping in both ts and py SDKs and add a test that asserts `request_id` is present on exception str/metadata? I can review today.

devex-bot: FYI: internal doc draft lives at https://redwood.dev/internal/sdks/errors — has recommended class names + examples. :link:

marta: one more question: token refresh concurrency — should SDK queue requests while refresh is in-flight or let them trigger refreshes? We're seeing duplicate refreshes from mobile clients causing rate-limits.

alex: Single-flight refresh (mutex + future/promise) is the recommendation. Other requests should await the in-flight refresh. If refresh fails, propagate AuthError to all waiting calls and log the failure with the originating request_id. Avoid retrying refresh in tight loops — use backoff.

luisa: Also: for 429s, implement exponential backoff with jitter and cap the retries. For streaming reconnects: exponential backoff + capped attempts; include request_id in reconnect logs so we can correlate across retries.

marta: Perfect — I'll draft the PR checklist: map codes -> exceptions, attach request_id to exceptions/logs, single-flight refresh, don't retry on 401, backoff on 429/5xx, stream errors carry partial data. Will ping when PR is up. :thumbsup:
